description: Bankside was once a secluded powerhouse of Victorian London, a place that kept industry in and casual visitors out. Today, it boasts a network of arches and alleyways repurposed for public use. Led by a Bankside insider, this tour explores the history and reclamation of the arch as a usable space through an emerging urban trail – including the brand-new America Street redevelopment.

factsheet.heading: About this walk
paragraphs: We will follow an emergent urban trail – The Low Line – exploring how these industrial elevated railway lines are being radically reimagined. Expect vibrant, usable public spaces, cultural hubs, and green corridors for the local community. Through a nuanced blend of urban design, local history, and contemporary placemaking strategy, this tour reveals how the historical bones of London are being repurposed to shape a sustainable future for the city.

factsheet.heading: About the guide
paragraphs: This walk is led be Leo Charleson, Placemaking Manager for Better Bankside; the local Business Improvement District.

factsheet.heading: Practical considerations
paragraphs: This walk will cover a fairly flat area in central London, though there may be some small steps and cobbles.

factsheet.heading: Golden Key Academy
paragraphs:
The Golden Key Academy is a course training up insightful and engaging guides dedicated to explaining London and bringing its many stories to life. This tour is part of a wider collection of tours created by Golden Key Academy guides for the Open House Festival celebrating their conclusion of the eight month course.  Further information on the Golden Key Academy can be found here https://open-city.org.uk/golden-key-academy
If you would like to attend this tour, please ensure you have booked a ticket before turning up.
